You are working on the Prompt Studio production codebase.

TASK:
Design and implement a production-grade AI credit system for Prompt Studio that works across multiple AI providers and models, including:

- Google Gemini
- OpenAI
- Anthropic Claude

The system must protect Prompt Studio from unexpected AI API costs while remaining simple for users.

IMPORTANT:
Before writing code, inspect the entire existing AI architecture.

Identify:
- Gemini integrations
- OpenAI integrations
- Anthropic/Claude integrations
- image generation
- video generation
- web generation
- prompt optimization
- agent/LLM workflows
- API routes
- server actions
- database models
- authentication/Clerk integration
- Stripe subscriptions
- existing credits/usage logic
- retries
- streaming
- background jobs
- webhook processing

Do not create a parallel system if credit or usage infrastructure already exists.
Refactor/extend the existing architecture.

CORE PRINCIPLE:

Users purchase Prompt Studio Credits.

Credits are NOT equivalent to tokens.

Different models and operations consume different amounts of credits based on the underlying API cost.

The server is the source of truth.

Never trust:
- model
- credit amount
- token count
- operation cost
- plan
- balance

when supplied by the client.

INITIAL PLANS:

Free:
1 initial credit

Creator:
$9/month
250 credits per billing cycle

Pro:
$19/month
1,000 credits per billing cycle

Studio:
$39/month
3,000 credits per billing cycle

Subscription credits should reset according to the billing-cycle rules.

Purchased/top-up credits must be tracked separately from subscription credits so expiration rules can be changed independently.

Do not silently expire purchased credits.

CREDIT PACKS:

Prepare the architecture for:

500 credits → $6
1,500 credits → $15
5,000 credits → $45
10,000 credits → $85

Stripe should be the authoritative payment source.

Credits must only be added after verified successful payment.

Use idempotent Stripe webhook processing so the same payment cannot add credits twice.

MODEL CREDIT SYSTEM:

Create centralized server-side model pricing/configuration.

Do NOT scatter credit values throughout components or API routes.

Example conceptual structure:

AI_MODEL_CONFIG = {
  provider,
  modelId,
  category,
  minimumCredits,
  inputTokenPrice,
  outputTokenPrice,
  imagePrice,
  videoPrice,
  enabled
}

The actual provider/model IDs must be discovered from the existing Prompt Studio integrations.

Do not invent model IDs.

INITIAL CREDIT MULTIPLIERS:

Economy / fast text models:
minimum 1 credit

Gemini Flash-class:
minimum 1 credit

Advanced Gemini Pro-class:
minimum 3 credits

Advanced OpenAI models:
minimum based on actual API cost

Premium OpenAI models:
minimum approximately 6 credits when current API economics justify it

Premium Claude models:
minimum approximately 8 credits when current API economics justify it

Image generation:
from approximately 10 credits

Premium image generation:
approximately 15–30+ credits

Video:
calculate separately based on provider, model, duration and resolution.

IMPORTANT:
These are initial business rules, NOT permanent hardcoded assumptions.

Verify the currently configured models and their billing characteristics.

The architecture must allow Prompt Studio to change model pricing without rewriting generation routes.

DYNAMIC CREDIT CALCULATION:

Do NOT simply implement:

GPT premium = always 6 credits

Instead implement a server-side cost-aware system.

Conceptually:

estimatedApiCost =
    inputTokenCost
  + outputTokenCost
  + imageCost
  + videoCost
  + providerSpecificCost

Then calculate credits using:

creditsRequired =
  max(
      modelMinimumCredits,
      ceil(estimatedApiCost / TARGET_COST_PER_CREDIT)
  )

Start with:

TARGET_COST_PER_CREDIT = $0.005

but make this centrally configurable.

Do not expose this internal cost constant to users.

The purpose is to prevent very large prompts or expensive operations from being charged the same as small requests.

TOKEN ESTIMATION:

Where provider APIs support token counting or usage estimation, use the provider-supported mechanism.

Otherwise use a conservative server-side estimate.

After generation, record the actual provider usage returned by the API whenever available.

Store both:

estimated_cost
actual_cost

This will allow Prompt Studio to measure profitability.

CREDIT RESERVATION:

Implement:

estimate → reserve → execute → reconcile

Before calling an AI provider:

1. Authenticate user.
2. Validate selected model.
3. Estimate credits.
4. Check balance.
5. Reserve required credits atomically.
6. Execute provider request.
7. Read actual usage.
8. Reconcile reserved credits against actual usage.
9. Persist usage transaction.

If generation fails because of Prompt Studio/provider infrastructure:
release/refund the reservation according to a documented policy.

Do not allow concurrent requests to overspend the same balance.

DATABASE:

Use the existing database architecture.

Implement an immutable credit ledger rather than only storing:

user.credits = 1000

Conceptually support transactions such as:

SUBSCRIPTION_GRANT
TOPUP_PURCHASE
AI_RESERVATION
AI_USAGE
REFUND
ADJUSTMENT
EXPIRATION

Each transaction should contain where appropriate:

id
userId
type
amount
balance impact
provider
model
operation
inputTokens
outputTokens
estimatedApiCost
actualApiCost
creditsCharged
requestId
stripePaymentId
metadata
createdAt

Never store API keys in these records.

BALANCE:

Provide a safe server-side function such as:

getCreditBalance(userId)

If subscription and purchased credits have different expiration behavior, expose:

subscriptionCredits
purchasedCredits
totalCredits

Define which balance is consumed first.

Recommended:
consume expiring subscription credits before purchased credits.

USER EXPERIENCE:

Before generation display:

"Estimated cost: 6 credits"

After generation:

"6 credits used · 742 credits remaining"

For variable operations use:

"From 6 credits"

until the final estimate is known.

Model selector examples:

Gemini Fast
From 1 credit

Gemini Advanced
From 3 credits

OpenAI Advanced
From X credits

Claude Advanced
From X credits

Never expose API dollar cost to normal users.

INSUFFICIENT BALANCE:

If credits are insufficient:

Do NOT call the provider API.

Return a typed error.

UI should display:

"You need X credits for this generation. You currently have Y."

Buttons:

"Buy credits"
"Upgrade plan"

CREDIT PACK PURCHASES:

Implement or prepare Stripe one-time purchases:

500 → $6
1,500 → $15
5,000 → $45
10,000 → $85

Do not grant credits based on the browser redirect/success page.

Only grant after verified Stripe webhook confirmation.

Ensure webhook idempotency.

COST PROTECTION:

Implement configurable safety limits:

- maximum tokens per request
- maximum estimated API cost per request
- maximum credits per generation
- per-user generation rate limit
- daily abuse protection
- model-specific limits
- image resolution limits
- video duration limits

Expensive requests must be rejected or require explicit user confirmation.

OBSERVABILITY:

For every AI operation record:

provider
model
operation
credits charged
estimated API cost
actual API cost
input tokens
output tokens
latency
success/failure

Create server-side metrics enabling calculation of:

AI revenue
AI cost
AI contribution margin
average cost per generation
average credits per generation
cost per active user
credits consumed per user
margin by model
margin by provider
margin by subscription plan

The key business metric should be:

AI contribution margin =
revenue attributed to AI usage - actual AI provider cost

Add an admin/reporting path or reusable query/service for these metrics if an admin analytics architecture already exists.

SECURITY:

- Provider API keys server-side only
- Never trust client credit balances
- Atomic credit deductions
- Idempotent webhook processing
- Idempotent generation requests where practical
- Protect against replay attacks
- Protect against concurrent overspending
- Rate limiting
- Validate model IDs server-side
- Never allow client-defined credit cost
- Log financial/credit mutations safely
